items.stem: Mendel took tall pea plants and short pea plants and produced F₁ progeny through cross-fertilization. What did Mendel observe in the F₁ progeny?
items.answer: Mendel observed that all pea plants were tall in F₁ progeny. This meant that only one of the parental traits (tallness) was dominant over the other one (dwarfness).
items.ocr: Printed answer line read 'Ans b OD 2018'; the stray 'b' is an OCR artefact of the answer-key marker and was dropped. LaTeX $F_{1}$ / $F_{1}^{\prime}$ rewritten as F₁.

items.stem: A Mendelian experiment consisted of breeding pea plants bearing violet flowers with pea plants bearing white flowers. What will be the result in F₁ progeny?
items.answer: All the progeny of F₁ generation will have violet flowers because violet colour is dominant over the recessive white colour.

items.stem: What is the source of hereditary information in the cell?
items.answer: DNA.
items.ocr: Printed 'hereditary informations'; kept as standard singular 'information'.

items.stem: Name the characters which show their existence in F₁ generation.
items.answer: Dominant characters.

items.stem: What is DNA?
items.answer: DNA is a genetic biomolecule which is the carrier of hereditary information from parents to the next generation.

items.stem: In which year was Mendel's work rediscovered?
items.answer: Mendel's work was rediscovered in 1900 after his death.

items.stem: Who coined the term 'gene'?
items.answer: The term 'gene' was coined by Johansen in 1909.

items.stem: How is the male produced?
items.answer: When a Y chromosome from the father fertilizes the ovum of the female, then a male (boy) is produced.

items.stem: What is heredity?
items.answer: The transmission of genetic characteristics from one generation to another is known as heredity.

items.stem: Name two dominant characters in pea plant.
items.answer: (a) Tallness, (b) Roundness of seeds.

items.stem: Write the name of two recessive characters in pea plant.
items.answer: (a) Shortness, (b) Wrinkleness of seeds.

items.stem: What is variation?
items.answer: Variation is the occurrence of smaller differences among the individuals of the same species, e.g., the offspring of the same parents do not exactly resemble each other or their parents.

items.stem: When pure breed tall pea plants of genotype TT are cross-bred with pure breed dwarf pea plants having genotype tt, all tall pea plants having genotype Tt are obtained in the F₁ generation. What will be the genotype ratio between TT, Tt and tt in the F₂ generation?
items.answer: TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1.
items.ocr: Answer key printed '$\mathrm{Tr}:\mathrm{Tt}:\mathrm{tt}=1:2:1$'; 'Tr' is an OCR misread of the homozygous dominant genotype TT named in the question stem, so it was repaired to TT. LaTeX F subscripts rewritten as F₁ / F₂.

items.stem: In which type of reproduction are more variations seen? Or, which type of reproduction causes greater diversity?
items.answer: Sexual reproduction.

items.stem: Name the biological term used to show similarities among individuals. Or, give one word for the following: "resemblances among individuals related by descent".
items.answer: Heredity.

items.stem: Write the expanded form of DNA.
items.answer: Deoxyribonucleic Acid.

items.stem: What are the characters which do not show their existence in F₁ generation called?
items.answer: Recessive characters.

items.stem: Write the sex chromosome in woman and man.
items.answer: In woman, XX; in man, XY.

items.stem: Define mutation.
items.answer: Sudden changes in the genetic form of an organism which are passed on to the next generation are called mutations.

items.stem: Name the first Indian medical practitioner who was aware of the concepts of genetics.
items.answer: Charaka was the first Indian medical practitioner who knew the factors which determine the sex of the child.
items.ocr: Printed answer line read 'Ans b Delhi 2013'; the stray 'b' is an OCR artefact of the answer-key marker and was dropped.

items.stem: Which of the following traits are recessive in pea plant? Dwarfness, violet flower, wrinkled seed.
items.answer: Dwarfness and wrinkled seeds are the recessive characters.
items.ocr: Printed answer line read 'Ans b Delhi 2014'; the stray 'b' is an OCR artefact of the answer-key marker and was dropped. Kept as very_short because the three traits are printed inline in the stem, not as lettered options.

items.stem: How is the female produced?
items.answer: When a sperm with X chromosome from the father fertilizes the egg, then a female (girl) is produced.

items.stem: How many types of chromosomes are there in the cell?
items.answer: There are two types of chromosomes in the cell: (i) sex chromosomes, and (ii) autosomes.

items.stem: Do a tailless mice have a tailless progeny?
items.answer: No, because removal of the tail, which is an acquired trait, cannot change the genes of the germ cells of mice.
items.ocr: Printed 'a quired trait'; repaired to 'acquired trait'.

items.stem: Name the biological term used to show differences among individuals.
items.answer: Variation.

items.stem: How many pairs of chromosomes are present in human beings?
items.answer: 23 pairs.

items.stem: Name the type of chromosomes which helps in the determination of sex in an organism.
items.answer: Sex chromosomes or allosomes.

items.stem: What are traits?
items.answer: The characters in individuals are called traits.

items.stem: In a mono-hybrid cross a round seeded plant was crossed with a wrinkle seeded plant. In F₂ generation genotype ratio obtained was 1 : 2 : 1. How many plants were homozygous round?
items.answer: A quarter of the plants (25%) were homozygous round.
items.ocr: LaTeX F subscript rewritten as F₂ and the percent macro as a plain % sign.

items.stem: Name the plant on which Mendel performed his experiments.
items.answer: Mendel performed his experiments on garden pea (Pisum sativum).

items.stem: What is F₂ generation?
items.answer: The generation produced by the offsprings of F₁ generation, i.e., with the first generation as parent, is called F₂ or second generation.
items.ocr: LaTeX F subscripts rewritten as F₁ / F₂.

items.stem: (a) What is the genetic constitution of human sperm? (b) Mention the chromosomes pair present in zygote determining the sex of a male child.
items.answer: (a) 22 + Y or 22 + X. (b) 22 + Y and 22 + X, or 44 + XY.
items.ocr: Printed stem read 'determing'; kept as standard 'determining'. LaTeX chromosome constitutions rewritten as plain text.

items.stem: Define a gene.
items.answer: A gene is a segment of functional DNA on a chromosome occupying a specific position which codes for a specific trait or protein synthesis. As such, it is a heredity determinant or a unit of genetic information.

items.stem: What are inherited traits?
items.answer: The characters which are transferred from one generation to the next generation are called inherited traits. This phenomenon is called inheritance.

items.stem: What are acquired characters or traits?
items.answer: The characteristics in an individual which are not inherited from the parents are called acquired characters. An individual acquires these traits from nature.
